## Native video and composition workflows

_From `src/agent_tools/sections/bun-video.md`._

`Bun.Video` is the native video API of the Aphrody runtime. Its Rust FilmCraft
provider decodes media; extracted frames reuse the `Bun.Image` transformation
and encoding pipeline. Use the global classes for metadata, thumbnails, raw
RGBA, bounded frame batches, PCM audio, GIF and MP4 remux.

```ts
if (!Bun.Video.available) throw new Error("Native video provider unavailable");
const video = new Bun.Video("input.mp4");
const metadata = await video.metadata();
await video.frame(1).resize(640).jpeg({ quality: 85 }).write("preview.jpg");
const frames = await video.frames({ start: 0, end: 3, step: 1, maxFrames: 3 });
for (const frame of frames) await Bun.write(`frame-${frame.time}.png`, frame.bytes);
await video.remux("new-output.mp4");
```

For a transformed frame without encoding, use
`await video.frame(seconds).resize(width, height).rgba()`. It returns owned
RGBA8 pixels with dimensions and four channels. Frame transformations follow
`autoOrient → extract → rotate → flip/flop → resize → modulate`.
Repeated fluent setters replace the previous setting. `metadata()` describes
the source; `width` and `height` describe the last completed transformed frame.

Preserve these boundaries when choosing operations:

- `frames` returns source-resolution PNGs, with an exclusive `end`, at most
  64 frames and 64 MiB per batch. Use `frame(time)` for individual transforms.
- `audio` returns PCM16 WAV, limited to 30 seconds and 64 MiB. `gif` is
  palette-quantized and limited to five seconds, 120 frames, 640×360 and 32 MiB.
- `remux` copies encoded packets into a new .mp4, .mov, .mkv or .webm (by extension; MP4 to MP4 keeps access units byte for byte) and `hls` cuts CMAF segments plus a VOD playlist; both refuse overwriting.
  `.png/.jpeg/.webp/.heic/.avif` select still-image output for frame terminals.
- Local path input uses bounded reads, with a 64 GiB file limit; memory input
  is limited to 256 MiB. Validate caller-supplied file paths before opening them.
- `Bun.Video.available` reports linked provider inclusion. Codec profiles,
  platform behavior and HEIC/AVIF output require their own qualification.
  `Bun.Video.backend` shares Image's transform backend, not a decoder selector.

Use `@aphrody/bun-video` for Remotion/HyperFrames compositions, HLS/DASH/MPD,
HAR inspection, browser capture, yt-dlp and optional FFmpeg/mpv adapters.
Those adapters have separate media SDK, browser, Python or license requirements.
Read the corresponding guide in `packages/bun-video/docs` before changing it.
WGSL analysis and browser/GPU availability do not establish hardware video
decoding, sustained encoding performance or DRM playback.

`@aphrody/bun-video/webgpu` and `bun-video webgpu` expose bounded compute:

```sh
bun-video webgpu info
bun-video webgpu probe
bun-video webgpu run shader.wgsl input.bin output.bin --backend native
```

Read `docs/runtime/video.mdx`, `docs/runtime/image.mdx` and the declarations in
`packages/bun-types/bun.d.ts`. Source owners are `src/runtime/video`,
`src/runtime/image` and `packages/bun-video/native/src/filmcraft.rs`.
For package compute, read `packages/bun-video/docs/webgpu.md` and
`docs/project/bun-video-webgpu.md`. `docs_search`/`docs_read` of `bun mcp`
provide the runtime reference; `examples_search` with `Bun.Video frame metadata`
selects source-backed examples from the installed dataset.

Use `bun bd test test/js/bun/video/video.test.ts` and the relevant Image tests for
native changes. Qualify stage manifests, SDK linkage, codecs, browser capture,
compute and encoding separately on each release target. Keep cookies, HAR
captures, credentials, datasets and signed media URLs in their protected stores.
